why.B1.1: Three-vessel involvement on CCTA and severe ischemia on PET-MPI are highly specific for three-vessel obstructive coronary artery disease
why.B2.1: Chronic stable angina is less likely due to the presence of severe ischemia on PET-MPI, which is more consistent with obstructive coronary artery disease
why.B3.3: Three-vessel obstructive coronary artery disease is less likely in the context of cardiomyopathy, but the evidence still supports this diagnosis
why.B4.1: Three-vessel obstructive coronary artery disease is possible, but the evidence is less specific in the context of other cardiac conditions
why.B5.2: Three-vessel obstructive coronary artery disease is less likely in the context of non-cardiac conditions, but the evidence still supports this diagnosis

sub_branches.label: Chronic Stable Angina
sub_branches.why_included: The patient's symptoms of substernal chest pain and the results of the Exercise Treadmill Test (ETT) and subsequent testing are consistent with chronic stable angina.

sub_branches.label: Microvascular Angina
sub_branches.why_included: The patient's symptoms of exertional chest pain and the results of the PET-MPI showing severe ischemia in the distribution of the left anterior descending and circumflex arteries are consistent with microvascular angina.

sub_branches.label: Variant Angina
sub_branches.why_included: The patient's symptoms of chest pain at rest and the results of the Coronary Angiogram showing 3-vessel involvement are consistent with variant angina.
